lia: that PR touched the batching scheduler, right? @ryan is owner of #5123 — can you check whether the scheduler change could affect tail latency?

ryan: yep that was me. it replaced the spin-wait with a scheduled yield path. intended to reduce CPU, but maybe we introduced head-of-line contention. I'll start a bisect on the staging commit range. can someone link the flamegraphs + perf script?

maya: flamegraph here: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/7421/flamegraph.svg and full logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/artifacts/7421/logs.txt
repro command: `RUN_BENCH=1 make bench-nightly ARTIFACT=7421`

sam: try this minimal repro to rule out platform variance (run on a single GPU, small batch):
```
export RW_BENCH_SAMPLE=small
make bench --target=runtime --gpus=1 --iterations=100
```
Also run `perf record -F 99 -g --` during the run and upload the `perf.data`

ryan: running the small repro now on gpu-staging-02. ping me if you need access to the cluster, creds are the usual ephemeral jump (ttl 1h).

lia: i'll watch kernel/sys settings — just fyi we deployed a minor kernel backport to gpu-prod last week. may be worth checking NUMA and CFS tunables.

maya: quick mitigation proposal: either revert #5123 for tonight or enable legacy scheduler via runtime flag. fallback path less disruptive if flag is trivial to flip. thoughts? :thinking_face:

sam: flag route preferred for speed. runtime flag env: `RW_BATCH_SCHED=legacy` — can be set via rollout route on dedicated pools. steps: 1) set flag for 10% of traffic 2) observe p95 3) widen if stable. I can patch rollout in Console if we agree.

ryan: i'll try the runtime flag first and run the repro. if that doesn't bring p95 down within 15 mins i'll open a revert PR.

maya: can you update here once you have numbers? aim to contain by 03:30 UTC. tagging oncall. :hourglass_flowing_sand: @oncall-bot
